Ford Madox Ford, The Fifth Queen.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/ford-madox-ford/the-fifth-queen

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Ford Madox Ford, the author, died 1939 (Wikidata Q537112, P570 = 1939-06-26).

First publication of the text used: 1906 (SE colophon: 'The Fifth Queen was published in 1906 by Ford Madox Ford.'; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Queen lists the United Kingdom as the country and Alston Rivers as the publisher).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1906, before 1931. A work published in 1906 entered the United States public domain on 1 January 2002. Standard Ebooks states the same in its rights statement below.
- Country of origin (United Kingdom): the text was first published there in 1906. Copyright lasts life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die did so in 1939, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 2010.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

- Wikidata Q537112 (Ford Madox Ford), P570 = 1939-06-26
